submission.justification:
Algorithm-L2 has the highest recorded signal efficiency in the 20-60 GeV scan: 92.6% at 35 GeV on the coarse scan and 92.9% at 34 GeV on the fine scan. Algorithm-L1 peaks at 74.7% and Algorithm-L3 at 85.9%. All three candidates were confirmed deployable in L1 hardware, and the threshold lies inside the allowed range.

The 34 GeV value should be treated as provisional. Its margin over neighbouring points is within the observed noise. The 33-37 GeV plateau averages 91.9%. The 35 GeV point measured 92.6% on the first run and 91.3% on the rerun, a 1.3-point discrepancy. The 34 GeV number is the maximum of a noisy scan, so the true efficiency there is probably close to the plateau average, not 92.9%.

Two gaps keep this from being a fully verified result. First, no trigger rate was recorded for any threshold, so I cannot confirm that the 8 kHz allocation is met at 34 GeV. Second, latency and granularity are unverified for all three candidates. Before committing, the rate at 33-37 GeV should be measured with enough events to resolve the efficiency differences, and the latency/granularity check should be completed.</justification>
